```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

First I must load the datasets into my R markdwon file 
``` {r}
rep_2018 <- read_csv("00_rep_candidates_2018.csv")
rep_2022 <- read_csv("00_rep_candidates_2022.csv")
dem_2018 <- read_csv("00_dem_candidates_2018.csv")
dem_2022 <- read_csv("00_dem_candidates_2022.csv")
polarization <- read_csv("00_polarization_congress.csv")
```
Next it's time to start cleaning names 
```{r}
rep_2018 <- rep_2018 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

rep_2022 <- rep_2022 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

dem_2018 <- dem_2018 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

dem_2022 <- dem_2022 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()
```
Now to drop columns


```{r}
rep_2018 <- rep_2018 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

rep_2022 <- rep_2022 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

dem_2018 <- dem_2018 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

dem_2022 <- dem_2022 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)
```
Next check the amount of rows/columns and make sure everything looks good

```{r check-clean}
glimpse(rep_2018)
glimpse(rep_2022)
glimpse(dem_2018)
glimpse(dem_2022)
```
